brief: Goldman's TMT desk note recaps a violent post-midterm week and frames Monday's open. Futures rebounded (Nasdaq +50bps, S&P +60bps, Russell +125bps) on hopes of Iran de-escalation (oil -3.5%) and despite NVDA's board launching an investigation after a CEO-affair headline (NVDA -5% premarket); hyperscalers (AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT) bid up while levered-datacenter plays (CRWV, IREN, NBIS) stayed pressured. The core thread: the Nov 3 election raised uncertainty over datacenter build pace in states like Texas, driving a semiconductor selloff (SOX -13% on the week, -31% since Oct 1, -28% over 22 sessions) that Goldman now calls oversold with compelling risk/reward, while its NVDA 3Q preview stays Buy-rated on power/funding/demand debates. Underneath, Prime flows show the deleveraging: Info Tech was the most net-sold global sector (matching 2016-era extremes), US Info Tech allocation fell to a 14.4% multi-year low, and systematic/CTA signals turned negative, with $28bn-$45bn of forecast SPX futures selling. Thursday's vol reversal was historic: the panic index hit 9.57, the 3rd-largest jump ever, after clients stripped hedges into Wednesday's rally, and ETFs printed their 3rd-largest notional volume day ever.
